turns.text: Rapid urbanisation is arguably reshaping South Asian societies more profoundly than any other trend at the moment.
On the one hand, cities concentrate opportunities, so migrants from rural areas can access jobs and education they'd never otherwise have.
On the other hand, infrastructure simply hasn't kept pace, which is why we see informal settlements springing up on the outskirts.
What concerns me most is that planning tends to be reactive; authorities address problems only once they've become unmanageable.
If I had to prioritise one policy, it would be investing in mid-sized cities, so that the pressure on megacities like Karachi eases somewhat.
